defects.note: Load, clone, Store is not atomic as a whole: the config watcher and the admin API each clone the same map and the later Store drops the other's route. Every access is atomic, so -race reports nothing. Serialize writers with a sync.Mutex (readers stay lock-free) or retry with CompareAndSwap
the same lost update as Set: a Delete racing a Set can resurrect the removed route or drop the new one; one writer mutex covers both

a Transport literal with DialContext or TLSClientConfig is not offered HTTP/2 unless ForceAttemptHTTP2 is set (or Protocols names HTTP/2): the HTTP2 config is ignored and every call goes over HTTP/1.1, against the doc comment. Clone http.DefaultTransport, or set ForceAttemptHTTP2: true

SendPingTimeout is zero, so the client never health-checks the connection: when a NAT or load balancer drops it silently, every multiplexed watch stream hangs for hours with no error. Set SendPingTimeout (and PingTimeout)

VerifyPeerCertificate is not called on resumed sessions and session tickets are on by default, so a client revoked after its first handshake keeps resuming for the ticket's lifetime, against 'must stop working on the next connection'. Move the check to VerifyConnection (cs.PeerCertificates[0]), which runs on every handshake

baits.note: since Go 1.27 Close drains an unread HTTP/1 body up to 256 KiB / 50 ms; closing is the whole obligation on a non-200
one Load per lookup reads a consistent snapshot that no one mutates; readers need no lock
